adapters.name: HTTP/API access log
capabilities: request rate by route, method, principal and source address
status-code outcomes including auth failures and rate limits
pagination/offset parameters and response byte counts
sensitive/protected route matching
limitations: only sees traffic that reaches an instrumented app or reverse proxy that writes an access log
cannot observe requests blocked upstream by a CDN/WAF unless those logs are also collected
log timestamps are trusted as supplied by the writer

adapters.name: Windows listening ports
capabilities: enumerates TCP listeners with owning PID and process name
diffs against a persisted baseline to surface new listeners
records both newly added and removed listeners as evidence
limitations: baseline is established on first successful poll; pre-existing listeners are not retroactively reported
UDP listeners are not covered
short-lived listeners between polls can be missed
process name can be null for protected processes without elevation

adapters.name: Windows process creation
adapters.reason: requires Windows process telemetry; host is linux
capabilities: process creation with image, parent, user and PID
command line when the 4688 policy includes it
flags images launched from temporary directories
limitations: 4688 requires "Audit Process Creation" success auditing and a Security log read permission
CIM fallback is a snapshot diff and misses processes that start and exit between polls
command lines are truncated and credential-shaped text is redacted before storage

adapters.name: Windows Security log (logon events)
adapters.reason: disabled in config; enable only where Security log access is authorized
capabilities: failed logons (4625) with source address, account and logon type
successful logons (4624) and logoffs (4647)
special privileges assigned (4672)
sensitive privilege use (4673) with process and service name
limitations: requires an elevated account with Security log read access
requires the matching audit policy subcategories to be enabled
cannot see domain-controller-side events unless this host is the DC

adapters.name: Windows Defender detections
adapters.reason: requires Windows Defender event log; host is linux
capabilities: Defender detection events (1116/1117) and configuration changes (5007)
limitations: only reports what the Defender operational log records
message parsing is best-effort because the event schema is not stable across Defender versions
does not replace EDR telemetry

adapters.name: Monitored application/config directories
capabilities: SHA-256 baseline of configured files and directories
created/modified/deleted change events
limitations: polling, so a change that is reverted between polls is not seen
bounded to 5000 files and 32MB per file
does not use the Windows USN journal (no extra privilege requirement)

adapters.name: Windows persistence (registry, scheduled tasks, WMI)
capabilities: registry value changes (4657) for audited persistence keys
scheduled task creation, deletion, disable and update (4698/4699/4700/4702)
WMI permanent event subscriptions (WMI-Activity 5861)
limitations: 4657 requires Audit Registry and a SACL on the monitored key
4698/4702 require Audit Other Object Access Events
WMI-Activity operational log must be enabled and readable
Sysmon registry events are covered separately by host.sysmon

adapters.name: Windows file access audit (4663)
capabilities: file read/write/delete access with process and account
object path and access mask from the Security log
complements hash-based host.files polling with access events
limitations: requires Audit File System policy and a SACL on each monitored path
4663 is generated only when the object SACL matches the access
security log volume can be high on busy file servers
does not capture file contents

adapters.name: Sysmon endpoint telemetry
capabilities: process creation including short-lived processes (event 1)
network connection metadata (event 3)
DNS queries (event 22)
file creation (event 11), registry changes (12/13/14)
WMI filter/consumer/binding persistence (19/20/21)
image loads, process access, injection and process tampering (7/8/10/25)
limitations: requires Sysmon installed and its operational log readable
event 3 is connection metadata, not packet contents
event 22 is DNS client telemetry, not a network sensor
Sysmon configuration controls which events exist at all

adapters.name: Windows DNS Client queries
capabilities: DNS query names, types, status and results from the DNS Client operational log
limitations: the DNS Client log records client lookups, not all DNS traffic on the wire
requires the Microsoft-Windows-DNS-Client/Operational log to be enabled and readable
Sysmon event 22 is preferable when Sysmon is already deployed

adapters.name: Cloud control-plane audit log (exported)
adapters.category: C: Data stores and external services
capabilities: AWS CloudTrail, Azure Activity and GCP Audit Log records exported to JSONL
principal, source address, action, resource and error outcome
privilege and IAM policy changes are scored
limitations: requires the provider audit export to be delivered to a readable file; this adapter holds no cloud credentials
export latency and retention are controlled by the provider
JSONL only: one audit record per line, or a single CloudTrail Records object per line

adapters.name: SQL Server live sessions and requests
adapters.category: C: Data stores and external services
capabilities: live user sessions and active requests from sys.dm_exec_sessions/sys.dm_exec_requests
statement text for active requests (truncated and redacted)
read/write/logical-read counters and blocking sessions
limitations: requires Windows, a SQL Server client assembly and an account with VIEW SERVER STATE
polling sees a request only while it is active; very short statements can be missed
does not capture historical statements unless the statement is still active
integrated security or a connection string in an environment variable; no password is stored in config

adapters.name: Third-party SaaS audit API
adapters.category: C: Data stores and external services
capabilities: authenticated HTTPS pull from a SaaS audit endpoint
principal, source address, action, resource and failure outcome
cursor-based since parameter when the provider supports it
limitations: requires the operator to supply an API token in an environment variable; this build stores no SaaS credential
provider-specific pagination beyond the configured response path is not implemented
the provider must expose an audit/event endpoint authorized for the token

adapters.name: Database audit log (exported)
adapters.category: C: Data stores and external services
capabilities: bulk reads measured by rows_returned / rows_read
privilege changes (GRANT/REVOKE/role changes) when exported
database authentication failures when exported
principal, source host, statement type and target table
limitations: no live database connection: requires pgAudit / MySQL audit / provider audit log exported to JSONL
if database auditing is not enabled upstream, this adapter sees nothing and must report NOT CONFIGURED
does not inspect query result contents

adapters.name: Reverse proxy / CDN / WAF access log
adapters.category: C: Data stores and external services
capabilities: edge request rate, status and byte counts
WAF action and rule identifiers when the provider exports them
source address as seen by the edge
limitations: requires the provider to export logs to a readable file; no provider API credentials are held by this service
log delivery latency varies by provider (Cloudflare Logpush is near-real-time but not synchronous)
requests dropped before the edge logger are invisible

adapters.name: Network sensor flow, DNS and TLS metadata
adapters.category: C: Data stores and external services
capabilities: per-flow byte counts and connection state (Zeek conn / Suricata flow)
DNS query names, types, answers and response codes
TLS SNI, negotiated version/cipher and certificate subject/issuer (not plaintext)
HTTP metadata and IDS alerts when the sensor emits them
limitations: requires a sensor (Zeek or Suricata) writing JSONL; this build is not a packet-capture driver
TLS is metadata only: payloads are not decrypted and no TLS interception is performed
encrypted traffic volume is visible, but content and intent are not
sensor placement determines whether east-west or only perimeter traffic is visible

adapters.name: Webflow (exported logs)
adapters.category: C: Data stores and external services
adapters.reason: disabled in config; no Webflow audit integration is configured
capabilities: parses operator-exported request logs when a log_path is supplied
limitations: no authorized Webflow audit-log API integration exists in this build
no Webflow API token is collected or stored
without an exported log file this source is reported NOT CONFIGURED, not monitored

adapters.name: Monitoring-service health
capabilities: evidence store writability, chain head and size utilization
alert queue depth and delivery errors
process memory and event-loop lag proxy
disk free space on the state volume
limitations: reports the service's own health only; it cannot detect its own total failure (needs an external heartbeat)
disk free is read from the state directory volume only
only sees traffic that reaches an instrumented app or reverse proxy that writes an access log
cannot observe requests blocked upstream by a CDN/WAF unless those logs are also collected
log timestamps are trusted as supplied by the writer
baseline is established on first successful poll; pre-existing listeners are not retroactively reported
UDP listeners are not covered
short-lived listeners between polls can be missed
process name can be null for protected processes without elevation

blind_spots.reason: store.anchor.path and store.anchor.url are empty; chain-head rollback is detectable only on this disk
limitations: Configure store.anchor.path (for example a UNC share) or store.anchor.url so the evidence head is copied off-host

blind_spots.reason: Thresholds are tuning values, not guarantees; an uninstrumented service whose logs are not collected remains outside visibility.
limitations: Low-and-slow scraping that stays below every threshold is not detected
TLS metadata comes from network.sensor when configured; TLS payloads are never decrypted
Producer timestamps are compared with observed_at, not cryptographically attested
